react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites converge on a single dominant biological signal: arachidonic acid metabolism and downstream eicosanoid biosynthesis. This conclusion is supported across three orthogonal enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 3.1×10⁻¹⁵, fold-enrichment 2001×), Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring (p=2.5×10⁻⁴, full 8/8 compound overlap on the arachidonic acid network), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p=2.5×10⁻⁶). The cross-paradigm consensus is WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' (WikiPathways) / KEGG:hsa00590 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' (KEGG), further corroborated by Mummichog's separate hit on 'Leukotriene metabolism' (p=0.021). Arachidonic acid (CHEBI:15843) is the primary upstream substrate and driver metabolite: it feeds the 5-lipoxygenase branch (producing 5-HETE and leukotriene A4), the 12/15-lipoxygenase branch (producing 15-HETE), the cytochrome-P450 epoxygenase branch (producing 5,6-EET), and the cyclooxygenase branch (producing 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2). The concurrent elevation of all eight metabolites in the treatment group therefore reflects coordinated activation of multiple eicosanoid arms from a shared substrate pool, consistent with an inflammatory, oxidative-stress, or pharmacological perturbation that displaces arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids. The two non-eicosanoid phenyl derivatives (3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) were not enriched in any pathway and are interpreted as background.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Eight differentially abundant metabolites were queried across three orthogonal enrichment paradigms. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with FDR 3.11×10⁻¹⁵ and fold-enrichment 2001×; Mummichog m/z-direct activity returned Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as its top hit with p=1.68×10⁻⁴; MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned KEGG:hsa00590 as its top hit with p=2.49×10⁻⁶. These three independent methods agree on the same biological process under three different database namespaces. Five of the input compounds are members of Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167): arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, 15-HETE, and leukotriene A4. Arachidonic acid is the upstream substrate; its oxidation through the PTGS/cyclooxygenase branch (reaction R02377) and the ALOX5/5-lipoxygenase branch (reaction R03142) produces the downstream eicosanoids observed. The two phenyl-derivative compounds (3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) were not enriched in any pathway across any paradigm.

pathway_members.sqlite only indexes HUMAN1 + RECON2; for namespace 'WP', inspect the `metabolites_hit` list inside an EnrichmentResult (e.g. from run_ramp_enrichment) — it carries the method-specific compound roster

pathway_members.sqlite only indexes HUMAN1 + RECON2; for namespace 'MUMM', inspect the `metabolites_hit` list inside an EnrichmentResult (e.g. from run_ramp_enrichment) — it carries the method-specific compound roster
use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

The cross-paradigm consensus is WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' (WikiPathways) / KEGG:hsa00590 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' (KEGG), further corroborated by Mummichog's separate hit on 'Leukotriene metabolism' (p=0.021). Arachidonic acid (CHEBI:15843) is the primary upstream substrate and driver metabolite: it feeds the 5-lipoxygenase branch (producing 5-HETE and leukotriene A4), the 12/15-lipoxygenase branch (producing 15-HETE), the cytochrome-P450 epoxygenase branch (producing 5,6-EET), and the cyclooxygenase branch (producing 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2). The concurrent elevation of all eight metabolites in the treatment group therefore reflects coordinated activation of multiple eicosanoid arms from a shared substrate pool, consistent with an inflammatory, oxidative-stress, or pharmacological perturbation that displaces arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids. The two non-eicosanoid phenyl derivatives (3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) were not enriched in any pathway and are interpreted as background.
